Sarah Eckhardt

Democratic candidate for Comptroller of Public Accounts, Texas · Challenger

Texas state senator (District 14) and attorney

Sarah Eckhardt is the Democratic state senator for Texas Senate District 14 and has held the seat since 2020. Before that, she served as Travis County Judge and as a Travis County commissioner. She dropped her bid for Congressional District 10 in December 2025 to run for comptroller, won the Democratic nomination in the March 3, 2026 primary, and will face Republican Don Huffines on November 3, 2026.

Where Eckhardt stands

School vouchers (Education Freedom Accounts)
Proposes auditing Texas' $1 billion Education Freedom Accounts voucher program, which the comptroller's office runs, to look at who receives the money and how it is spent.
State contracting and corruption
Pledges to investigate and stop no-bid state contracts that she says go to wealthy donors, and to root out government corruption.
Role and independence of the office
Says the comptroller should act as a government watchdog, run an independent office, and give Texans and lawmakers clearer information about how state money is spent.
Medicaid expansion
Proposes using the office to report how much it costs Texas to refuse Medicaid expansion.
Data centers
Has backed a moratorium on data center development.
Professional licensing and immigration status
Opposes a change that requires proof of legal immigration status to get a professional license.
Comptroller fluoride review
Argues that the comptroller's office review of water fluoridation under Huffines is a misuse of state resources.
School spending review
Argues that the comptroller's school spending review goes beyond the agency's authority, and says foreign workers and library books fall outside the review's scope.

Background

  • Texas State Senator, District 14 (2020–present)
